_window: Notes written 26 Oct 2026 from 15 Sep – 14 Oct data; the numbers on the page recompute for any range, the notes do not.

INT-5033.title: Location access not given (Android)
INT-5033.npci: None. Not in the core translator (upi_config.response_code_translator); Paytm stops the payment before it is sent to NPCI, so there is no RIS code.
INT-5033.why: Paytm requires device location for every UPI International payment. App message: 'To complete this payment securely, please enable location access … Settings > Location > App Permissions'. INT-5033 is the Android variant (100% of its failures are Android).
evidence: 1,142 failures, ₹45.5 L failed GMV: the largest failure code (17% of all failures).
When the app sent no location (lat/long missing or 0,0) 57% of those payments failed with INT-5033; 42% of INT-5033 failures had no location at all.
The other 58% did send a location (in India) and were still blocked: likely the permission is 'approximate' / 'while using' only, or the location was stale. Check with the app team which check fires.
Spread across all payer banks and both handles (ptyes 81%, ptaxis 19%, same as volume), so it is not bank-driven. Older app builds fail more (10.83.12: 7.1% vs 3.9% on 10.85.5).

INT-5032.title: Location access not given (iOS)
INT-5032.npci: None. Not in the core translator; blocked inside Paytm before NPCI.
INT-5032.why: iOS variant of INT-5033. App message: 'enable location access … Settings > Privacy & Security > Location Services'.
evidence: 844 failures, ₹36.2 L failed GMV (13% of failures); 100% iOS.

No location sent: 24.5% of those payments failed with INT-5032. 73% of INT-5032 failures did send an India location, so the permission level (precise vs approximate) is the more likely trigger on iOS.
No payer-bank or handle concentration; app 10.85.5 fails least (0.8%) vs 6–8% on 10.83.10, 10.84.9, 10.85.6 and 10.86.0, so it is worth checking what changed between those builds.

INT-20123.title: Cooling period: new device / new bank link
INT-20123.npci: No NPCI code. The core translator maps it only to risk code RISK123 (Paytm risk), nothing is sent to NPCI.
INT-20123.why: UPI cooling-period rule: for 72 hours after a new device binding or bank-account link, payments are capped at ₹5,000 per 24 hours.
evidence: All 31 failures were within 72 h of device binding (hours since oauthDeviceBindingTime).
Mostly above ₹5,000 (12 of 31 in ₹5k–10k, 9 above ₹10k), consistent with the ₹5,000 cap; the few smaller ones are users who had already spent part of the ₹5,000.
HDFC payers are 55% of these failures; small numbers, so this may just be chance.

INT-1928.title: Cooling period (bank account / login)
INT-1928.npci: No NPCI code (translator row has no NPCI / CBS / risk code).
INT-1928.why: App message: the money transfer failed because the bank account was linked or the user logged in recently; same family as INT-20123 / INT-9661.
evidence: Use the 'hours since device binding' and amount panels for this code to see the cooling-period pattern.

INT-5176.title: Declined by receiver's bank
INT-5176.npci: No NPCI code on the txn; the core translator maps it to CBS code RECON_120 only.
INT-5176.why: App message: 'Your payment was declined by receiver's bank.' Check the payee handle / beneficiary bank split.

PM14.title: UPI International request timeout
PM14.npci: PM14 is itself an NPCI code (v2.9: 'Request timeout scenario for UPI International', BD).
PM14.why: The international leg (NIPL / partner network) did not answer in time.
evidence: 782 failures, 667 of them on 5–7 Oct (270, 254, 143) plus 90 on 9 Oct: this is the main cause of the 4–7 Oct SR dip.
Hit every partner in proportion (fonepay Nepal, RMA Bhutan, LankaPay, SBI Global) and every payer bank at ~2%, so it was a network-level outage, not one partner or one bank.

RESP_VAL_QR_NOT_FOUND.title: QR not found at the partner
RESP_VAL_QR_NOT_FOUND.npci: NPCI response RESP_VAL_QR_NOT_FOUND; Paytm app code U08 (System exception).
RESP_VAL_QR_NOT_FOUND.why: The partner network could not find the scanned merchant QR (expired / deregistered / wrong QR).
evidence: 303 failures, spread across Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka and Singapore partners in proportion to volume.

U16-01176.title: Nepal per-payment limit (₹35,000)
U16-01176.npci: NPCI code U16 (risk threshold exceeded) with NPCI subcode 01176; not in the core translator, so the subcode is the RIS reason.
U16-01176.why: App message: 'For merchant payments in Nepal, you can send up to Rs 35,000 at a time and Rs 1 lakh in 24 hours.' This is the NPCI / UPI International cap for Nepal merchant payments.
evidence: 178 failures in the full pull, ₹72.5 L failed GMV in 15 Sep – 14 Oct: every one is ₹28,750 or more (NPR 46,000+), all to Nepal (fonepay).
Failures below ₹35,000 are users who had already used part of the ₹1 lakh / 24 h limit.
Spread across SBIN, HDFC, ICIC, PUNB in proportion to volume, so it is an NPCI rule, not a bank's.

U31-XW.title: Compliance violation (beneficiary)
U31-XW.npci: U31 (credit leg) with XW: 'Transaction cannot be completed. Compliance violation (beneficiary)'.
U31-XW.why: The beneficiary side (fonepay Nepal) rejects the credit on compliance grounds.
evidence: 656 failures, 100% Nepal / fonepayaxis; the rate rises with ticket size (largest code in the ₹2k–10k bands).

U30-Z9.title: Insufficient funds
U30-Z9.npci: U30 (debit leg) with Z9: insufficient funds in the remitter account.
U30-Z9.why: The payer does not have enough balance (customer side).
evidence: 685 failures across all payer banks; BARB (3.1%) and IOBA (3.5%) are above the ~1.7% average.

U16-01188.title: Bhutan per-payment limit (₹25,000)
U16-01188.why: App message: 'For merchant payments in Bhutan, you can send up to Rs 25,000 at a time and Rs 1 lakh in 24 hours.'
evidence: All Bhutan (RMA). Median failed ticket ≈ ₹39,500, i.e. above the ₹25,000 cap.

U16-00980.title: ₹1 lakh per 24 hours
U16-00980.npci: U16-00980 (the core translator maps it to itself).
U16-00980.why: App message: 'You can send up to Rs 1 lakh in 24 hours.' The daily UPI limit across payments.

U16-01180.why: Count limit: 'You can make up to 50 merchant payments in Nepal in 7 days.' Small tickets, so not an amount issue.

U16-01423.title: Nepal high-value block (no app message)
U16-01423.npci: U16 with NPCI subcode 01423; not in the core translator and no app message in response_mapper.
U16-01423.why: Not documented. All 50 failures are Nepal and ₹50,250 or more (median ₹64,000), so it behaves like a high-value / cumulative Nepal limit (likely the NPR 1,00,000 ≈ ₹62,500 or ₹1 lakh / 24 h rule).
evidence: No Nepal payment of NPR 1,00,000 or more succeeds in the window.

INT-9661.title: Cooling period: new device / new bank link
INT-9661.why: Same rule as INT-20123: ₹5,000 every 24 hours for 72 hours after a new device or bank link.
